# ankra_api_token (Resource)

A personal API token of the provider token's user, in the current organisation. The counterpart of `ankra tokens create`; destroy revokes and then deletes it, like `ankra tokens revoke` followed by `ankra tokens delete`.

The token value is revealed once, at creation, and kept in state as a sensitive value. A personal token belongs to the user who minted it: if the provider later authenticates as someone else (a CI service token, say) or in another organisation, every plan stops with an error instead of losing track of the token and minting a second one.

**What changes the token value.** The platform cannot edit a token, so changing `expires_at`, `scopes` or `project_id` (and `name` or `label`) mints a new token value in place: the provider mints the replacement first and only then revokes and deletes the old token, so there is no window without a working token, but every holder of the old value must be given the new `token`. When the name stays the same, the provider first renews the old token (`-replaced-` suffix, 24 hours of overlap) to free the name. If minting then fails, the next apply finishes the re-mint. An old token that could not be revoked and deleted is retried on every later apply until it is gone. Nothing else re-mints the token.

**Drift.** A token revoked outside Terraform stays in state with `revoked = true` and is re-minted in place on the next apply (a revoked token cannot be renewed, so a personal token's revoked predecessor is deleted first, and a service token's account is kept alive by a short-lived bridge token meanwhile). A token renewed outside Terraform (`ankra tokens rotate`, which renames it `<name>-replaced-<stamp>`) stops every plan with an error naming what to do. A change of `expires_at`, `scopes` or `project_id` made outside Terraform re-mints the token on the next apply.

~> Do not compute `expires_at` from `timestamp()`, for example `timeadd(timestamp(), "720h")`: the value changes on every plan, so every apply mints a new token. Use a fixed date, or `time_offset` from the `time` provider.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An MCP token for an AI client; the value is in ankra_api_token.mcp.token.
resource "ankra_api_token" "mcp" {
  name       = "claude-desktop"
  expires_at = "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  scopes     = ["mcp:read"]
}

output "mcp_token" {
  value     = ankra_api_token.mcp.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Token name: letters, digits, spaces, `-`, `_` and `.`, at most 100 characters, unique among the user's tokens.

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) Expiry as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Defaults to 90 days after creation.
- `project_id` (String) Project the token is pinned to. Unset makes it organisation-wide; the provider always sends the choice, because the platform would otherwise pin an MCP token to whatever project the user last selected in the portal.
- `scopes` (Set of String) Permission allowlist: `mcp:read` and/or `mcp:write` make an MCP token, which ordinary REST requests refuse. Unset keeps the token at the full authority of its holder; an empty set is refused, because the platform reads it as unset.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time of the current token value.
- `id` (String) Token id. It changes whenever the token value is re-minted.
- `organisation_id` (String) Organisation the token was minted in.
- `owner_user_id` (String) User the token belongs to: the provider token's user when it was minted.
- `revoked` (Boolean) Whether the token needs re-minting: it was revoked outside Terraform, or an earlier re-mint was interrupted. The next apply re-mints it in place.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token value. Revealed only when minted; null after an import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# API tokens are imported by id. The token value cannot be recovered.
terraform import ankra_api_token.mcp 5b1c0d52-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
